page: 19 guides, fee references and one software page
change: Where a page lacked an official figure (for example AliExpress's commission rate, Amazon's Remote Fulfillment and removal rates, the Renewed and Amazon Business referral discounts, TikTok Shop reserve levels and FBA fees for a specific product), worked examples that had used illustrative stand-in numbers now use formulas in which the missing figure is a named input, and new sections explain what sets the cost and how to plan without it. A public IPI threshold (300 for FBA New Selection) was added to the IPI page. Date-bound wording on the Section 301, A2X and Q4 deal pages was rewritten so it stays accurate after those dates pass.
why: Never fill a missing official figure with an invented one; keep pages correct after their dates pass.

change: Expanded pages that relied on rules Amazon publishes only inside Seller Central with publicly documented detail: Selling Partner API report and field definitions, Amazon's own announcements and regulations. Each new statement was checked against its source in a separate pass; statements the sources did not support were removed. 76 pages received their own licensed photo instead of a shared one. Section 301 exclusion end date (November 9, 2026) re-checked against the Federal Register.
why: Make each page useful on its own; keep only what the sources support.

change: Pages at addresses from the earlier site were rewritten from scratch at the same URLs from primary sources: Amazon's, TikTok's, AliExpress's and Walmart's own published pages, US and EU regulations, and — on the seller software pages only — each vendor's own pages about its product. Four TikTok and Amazon pages whose topic could not be sourced publicly, and two overlapping peak-fee pages, now forward to the closest page.
why: Keep existing addresses working; primary sources only.

change: Site rebuilt from scratch. Every page was rewritten from primary sources and every fact rechecked in a separate, automated verification pass. Earlier guides that relied on secondary sources or on pages that require a login were withdrawn; where a rewritten page answers the same question, the old address forwards to it.

The "How we check" section said a named reviewer signs off on every page before release, and that vendors are never cited. It now says pages are drafted with AI writing tools and checked in a separate automated pass, that pages read by the editor say so with the date, and that software vendors are cited only for their own product and price.
why: The earlier wording did not match how pages are produced or the editorial standards.

change: Removed the statement that photos may come from Wikimedia Commons; every photo on the site is from Unsplash under the Unsplash License. Added the dates of the editor's two e-commerce roles.
why: Accuracy: the image register lists only Unsplash photos, and the two roles overlapped in time.

change: The green "Verified" date label on pages now reads "Sources checked". The cookie banner buttons were renamed "Allow personalized ads" and "Non-personalized ads", and the privacy and cookie policies now say that non-personalized ads still use cookies for frequency capping, reporting and fraud prevention.
why: Clearer wording: the check is automated, and "Essential only" overstated what refusing personalization does.

change: The hosting section said the site is served by GitHub Pages. It now names Cloudflare Pages (Cloudflare, Inc.), which actually hosts the site, links Cloudflare's privacy policy, and notes that Cloudflare can set a strictly necessary security cookie and hide email addresses from scrapers. The cookie policy table was updated the same way.
why: Accuracy: the site is published through Cloudflare Pages.

change: "Blogs are not cited" now reads "third-party blogs are not cited" and says that a marketplace's own seller blog or announcements page counts as that marketplace's publication; the About page and home page use the same wording.
why: Some Amazon rules are published on Amazon's own seller blog (sell.amazon.com/blog), which the earlier wording appeared to exclude.

change: The latest HTS revision is now 2026 HTS Revision 23, published November 10, 2026 (previously Revision 22, October 30, 2026).
